summary: `openCompletion({ trigger, query?, source? })` opens a completion list from code, e.g. a toolbar button: on `useChatComposer()`, `useChatComposerInput()` and the `RichMentionInput` handle. Closing the list untouched removes the inserted trigger again.
howTo: If your toolbar opens the `@` or `/` list by writing the trigger into the editor and dispatching a synthetic `new InputEvent('input')`, call `composer.openCompletion({ trigger: '@' })` from `useChatComposerInput()` (or `useChatComposer().openCompletion`, which waits until the composer is mounted) instead. It does nothing while the composer is locked (`canCompose` false, also on a disabled `RichMentionInput`). It focuses the editor, adds a space when needed, searches at once without the debounce, and `source: 'people'` limits the list to those provider ids (the composer's search and one made by `createCompletionSearch`; an own `onSearch` gets `(query, trigger)` only). Escape, an outside click, blur, an empty result, Enter before the results show (it sends nothing) or an inserted mention remove the text again when the user typed nothing. A custom `RichMentionInputHandle` implementation may add the optional `openCompletion`. `ChatComposerInputControls.openCompletion` and `ChatComposer.openCompletion` are required members, so hand-written mocks or fakes of these types must add them.
